messages.subject: Compiling a Nimble function
parts:
I apologize for asking what must be a fairly simple question, but I am stumped.  I have written a nimble function that implements Neal's algorithm 6 for nonparametric Bayes with DP's.  It runs and seems to give good answers, although there are the typical algorithm 6 issues with high dependencies.  It will perform a million iterations in a little over four hours on my machine, and I'd like to see how the performance changes when compiled.  When I attempt to compile, I get the following error:

Warning, mismatched dimensions in assignment: sgamma <- map("gamma", 1, call, list, list). Going to browser(). Press Q to exitFALSE
Called from: sizeAssignAfterRecursing(code, symTab, typeEnv)


It seems likely that I'm not passing appropriate information for the compiler, but I'm not sure how to proceed.  I've included a way to generate some data, the nimble code, and a sample call to the function.

Thanks for any help.


library(nimble)
y1 <- rgamma(10,shape=1,scale=1)
y2 <- rgamma(10,shape=5,scale=5)
y3 <- rgamma(10,shape=10,scale=10)
y4 <- rgamma(10,shape=20,scale=20)
y <- c(y1,y2,y3,y4)

Nalgo6GammaD <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(y=double(1),alpha=double(),loops=integer()){
  n <- length(y)
  pp <- alpha/(alpha+n-1)
  gamma <- matrix(5,loops,n)
  theta <- matrix(5,loops,n)
  sgamma <- matrix(5,1,n-1)
  stheta <- matrix(5,1,n-1)
  ans <- matrix(0,loops,2*n)
  for (j in 2:loops){
  for (i in 1:n){
    gamma[j,i] <- gamma[j-1,i]
    theta[j,i] <- theta[j-1,i]
    if (i==1){sgamma <- gamma[j-1,2:n]
              stheta <- theta[j-1,2:n]}

    if (i==n){sgamma <- gamma[j,1:(i-1)]
              stheta <- theta[j,1:(i-1)]
              }
          else {sgamma <- c(gamma[j,1:(i-1)],gamma[j-1,(i+1):n])
                stheta <- c(theta[j,1:(i-1)],theta[j-1,(i+1):n])}
    for (k in 1:25){
    ngamma <- rgamma(1,1.5,.1)
    ntheta <- rgamma(1,1.5,.1)
    if (runif(1,0,1) > pp){cnt <- length(sgamma)
                           k <- ceiling(cnt*runif(1,0,1))
                           ngamma <- sgamma[k]
                           ntheta <- stheta[k]}
  qnum <- dgamma(y[i],shape=ngamma,scale=ntheta,log=TRUE)
  qdenom <- dgamma(y[i],shape=gamma[j,i],scale=theta[j,i],log=TRUE)
  qq <- qnum - qdenom
  if (qq > log(runif(1,0,1))){
    gamma[j,i] <- ngamma
    theta[j,i] <- ntheta
               }
          }
  }
    ans[j,1:n] <- gamma[j,]
    ans[j,(n+1):(2*n)] <- theta[j,]

  }
    return(ans)
    returnType(double(2))
  }
)

chk <- Nalgo6GammaD(y,2,1000)

messages.subject: Re: Compiling a Nimble function
parts:
Hi Gil,

I think there are a couple of things going on here.

First, you are running into NIMBLE’s need for static types when compiling.  Specifically, you have created sgamma as a matrix, so it must remain a matrix.  When you do sgamma <- gamma[j-1,2:n], you are assigning a vector into a matrix, which is causing a problem.  Mimicking R, NIMBLE allows gamma[j-1, 2:n, drop = FALSE] so it will return a matrix instead of a vector, which you should be able to assign to a matrix.  (drop = FALSE means it will not drop a dimension due to the single index).  Another way to do it would be sgamma[1, 1:size] <- vector

Second, the current release of NIMBLE does not support c().  You have two choices.  c() and a variety of other core R features are supported on the devel branch of our github repository.  So if you want you can install nimble from there (library(devtools); install_github("nimble-dev/nimble", ref = "devel", subdir = "packages/nimble”).  Still the c() will return a vector so you would have to assign into a vector.  Another option (without installing from devel) is to assign into each piece of sgamma by a separate line instead of using c() to do it in one line.

Looks like the same issues may come up for some of your other variables.

Perry
